> 无眼界，乃至无意识界。无无明，亦无无明尽，乃至无老死，亦无老死尽。

Eighteen realms, then twelve links of dependent origination. Two classifications, and they are not two topics — they are two cages, and they have different shapes.

The eighteen realms are spatial. Eye, form, eye-consciousness; ear, sound, ear-consciousness; and so on through mind, mental object, mind-consciousness. Each triplet is a boundary drawn between inside and outside. 界 means boundary, domain, the line where one thing ends and another begins. Eighteen of them, and together they define the map of where you end and the world starts.

The twelve links are temporal. Ignorance, formations, consciousness, name-and-form, the six senses, contact, feeling, craving, grasping, becoming, birth, aging-and-death. A chain, with a first link and a last, and the whole of Buddhist practice organized around breaking it at the first.

## The second cage is the one practitioners build

The first cage is ordinary: everyone lives inside the eighteen realms, and the sutra's 无 says the boundary is not a self.

The second cage is built by people who have read the first half of the sentence.

If ignorance is the first link, then destroying ignorance is the exit. So the whole project becomes 破无明 — dismantle ignorance, then aging-and-death stops, then you are out. And this is a goal, an attainment, something to be achieved, with a person achieving it.

The line closes that too: 无无明，亦无无明尽. No ignorance — and no end of ignorance. The exit is sealed at both ends, because the exit was a piece of the cage.

Not because ignorance is not there. Because ignorance is a phase, not a substance; there is nothing solid enough in it to be destroyed. What looks like destroying it is the chain ceasing to be driven. 尽 is the name we give to that, afterward, from outside.

## What that does to the goal

It removes the one thing that made the practice feel like progress: a finish line.

The book's formulation is that 流转 is function and 尽灭 is also a provisional name — 流转是作用，尽灭也是假名. Which is uncomfortably close to saying: the thing you have been working toward is a word.

And then the useful part. If the goal is a word, the work is not cancelled — it is relocated. The chain still runs; the question becomes whether it runs driven or undriven. Craving arising is not the problem. Craving being handed the next link without a gap is.

## Laozi's version, and the difference

*夫物芸芸，各复归其根。归根曰静.* The ten thousand things flourish and each returns to its root; returning to the root is called stillness. That is the temporal cycle seen from outside, with a resting point at the end of it.

The book notes where the sutra goes further: not only is the cycle a provisional name, the returning is too. Laozi offers the root as a place to come back to. The sutra declines to let even that be a place — 归 is a motion, and motion has an edge.

## The test

Name the thing you are trying to eliminate in yourself. Not improve — eliminate. The habit, the fear, the reaction.

Then check: is there anything there solid enough to be eliminated, or is it a pattern that runs when conditions assemble? If it is a pattern, the operation available to you is not destruction. It is interruption, at the seam.
